newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rate cut buoys Australian stocks to new highs.
newsitem.headline: Rate cut buoys Australian stocks to new highs.

text.p: Australian stocks surged to another record high at the opening on Monday as sentiment remained buoyant after Friday's surprise interest rate cut by the Reserve Bank. Banks and insurers led the market.
The All Ordinaries index was up 9.1 points at 2,573.0 after the first half hour but off a intra-day record high of 2,577.7 set in the first few minutes of trading.
Brokers said volume was light with A$115.77 million (US$88.56 million) worth of market trade. They said most of the action was in interest rate sensitive stocks.

Despite the early surge, shares in market heavyweight Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd fell after it announced that trading conditions remained difficult and that it expected a flat performance until it restructured and new projects came on stream.
"The highlights are the banks after the rate cut," said Gordon Furner, a broker at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett.
Shares in Australia's largest bank, National Australia Bank, hit a record high of A$19, but eased in later trade.
Insurance stocks were also stronger, with FAI Insurances topping the turnover list with over 20 million shares traded. Brokers said the FAI trade was handled by Macquarie Equities.

The cut in offical cash rates by 0.5 percentage points to 5.5 percent by the RBA was seen as a boost for the housing market and consequently building material suppliers, brokers said. The housing market is looking to consolidate a recovery.
The Australian building materials index was the strongest riser but most indicies rose. Only the gold, telecommunications, alcohol and tobacco went against the positive trend.
